checks.name: central_question_resolved
checks.evidence: Central question: 'Can they steal the guild's ledger without becoming its new masters?' Ch 15: Devan takes the book and hands it to Neela before forty witnesses. Ch 18 and ch 25–26: she holds the pages 'until it's safe', and Chathu uses that delay to take the forty back. Ch 27: she breaks the hunt without reading a single page, and she takes Vellan's page from Devan's hand. Ch 28: she reads every page aloud by daylight and gives each one to its owner. She lets the forty choose how theirs is read, and she keeps 'nothing but her own name'. Pachan keeps the groves with 'no one the master'. The question is answered: they stole the ledger and neither became its master. Only the queen's thirty pages stay open, and that is the series hinge.

checks.name: clues_paid_off
checks.evidence: All 19 page-level clues pay off. C01 ch 32 (the langurs fall silent again, and Vellan confirms the escort crossed the closed pass). C02 ch 7 (the pouch is empty). C03 ch 32 (the seams were pared by a palace surgeon). C04 ch 32, implicitly: the escort are odiyans, which explains the whining hounds of ch 3 and ch 5. C05 ch 22/24 (Eravi buys Resin House medicines; the salve came from Fourth Guard). C06 ch 9 (the grey packet). C07 ch 30 (the stripping writ). C08 ch 32. C09 ch 14–15 (the box on the shaft ledge). C10 ch 28 (Pachan lifts the gate bar). C11 ch 24 (Eravi overheard the cart order). C12 ch 23. C13 ch 23–24 (the postern and the physician's key). C14 ch 20–21: the sunbird 'by leave' column shows the crown permits raids, and ch 21 ties Ittan's raiders to new, unhandled silver. This payoff is indirect; no character revisits the coin itself. C15 ch 16–18 (all eleven contracts told). C16 ch 32 ('Sold to the crown'). C17 ch 27 ('Release not to be granted. Sell to the crown when spent'). C18 ch 24, implicitly: the 'tapper I know' becomes Eravi's tapper's-widow supplier, but the wood-road ride itself is never mentioned again. C19 ch 20 (cipher key, 'Nellimala, second harvest' marked 'by leave'). C20, C21 and C22 are logged as series threads. Soft spots to watch: C04, C14 and C18 pay off by inference rather than on the page.

checks.name: midpoint_reversal
checks.evidence: Ch 16 is the midpoint. Neela reads aloud: 'Kettamala, the warden's daughter, the west stair. Buyer, the Keeper. Hand, Thirty. Lookout, Seventeen.' This recasts the parrot newel, the hollow eleventh step and her wide path around the stair from the first half. It changes the romance at once. Devan says 'I need to walk' and goes out into the rain without his cloak. Ch 17 follows with 'care without ease': he sleeps across the sill, takes the pebble, and says 'I won't answer that' when she asks whether he can look at her.

checks.name: heroine_belief_change
checks.evidence: Opening belief (ch 1, still argued in ch 18): 'I won't carry what was put in my hands in the dark. It isn't mine.' Ch 23 is the first choice she couldn't have made in ch 1. She confesses to Janu before giving any excuse, and when asked why she says: 'They made me, Janu... That's the true answer. It isn't a reason.' The decisive proof is in ch 29. She stands unasked at the assize and reads the line Devan had offered to read for her: 'Seventeen is a number. It was mine for twenty-one years. My name is Neela. I'm the lookout... I do not offer that as a reason.' Ch 28 shows the same change in power: she reads every page by daylight and keeps none. The outline names ch 28 as the proof chapter, but the clearest on-page proof is ch 29 (with ch 23 as setup).

checks.name: real_loss
checks.evidence: Ch 28: Neela reads Kirri's page through the bars of kennel nine and lays it by the anklet. 'Kirri stays a civet, and that stays lost.' The text says: 'A caging could not be undone, and a page in the straw could not undo it.' Ch 30: Devan is stripped of Kettamala and his office and hands the seal to Muthu. That loss holds through ch 31–32. Ittan (ch 5), Raiu, Asha and Ammu also stay dead.

checks.name: love_interest_goal
checks.evidence: Devan's goal is to put his sister Asha's murder on court record with paper proof (ch 1: 'I need that entry... A court will take paper'; ch 6). He held this goal six years before he met Neela. It pays off in ch 29: 'Asha, daughter of the late warden of Kettamala... Killed under contract. Her name is written.' The ch 16 reversal entangles Neela in the evidence, but the goal itself is independent of her.

checks.name: series_hinge
checks.evidence: Ch 32: they break the queen's green seal and find a sheet headed 'Sold to the crown' listing thirty numbers. The cut stubs in the ledger match those numbers. Vellan confirms that 'the queen's night-guard... Odiyans, all of them. Thirty', and that the four escort were among them. He also warns that the watcher's log will lead the household to the shelter by the new moon. The book ends with Neela binding herself to the forty's vote and the bigger question raised: 'Thirty pages sat in a chest in Kodiyur, under the hand of the one master they could not reach.'

series_threads.thread: First Guard's 'It passes' marks her as an odiyan who has survived the ache. Ch 32 identifies her as one of the queen's thirty night-guard; freeing her is a book 2 question.

Devan still holds the sunbird payment writ (the queen paid for his death) for a high court in full session. That court will no longer sit for a stripped warden, so the writ carries into book 2 as evidence against the queen.
The forty have one season of resin, nine tapping knives and Pachan's grove map, but the groves are behind them. The coming ache and the question of who supplies resin are open for book 2.

summary: The book meets all seven structural promises. The central question is answered in ch 27–28: the ledger is stolen, every page is read back by daylight, and neither lead keeps power. Only the queen's thirty pages stay open, and that hinge is set up in ch 32. The ch 16 'Lookout, Seventeen' reversal recasts the first half and visibly breaks the leads' ease. Neela's belief change is shown in her unexcused confession to Janu (ch 23) and in her unasked reading of the lookout line at the assize (ch 29). Kirri staying a civet and Devan's lost office are real, permanent losses. Devan's goal of putting Asha's murder on record predates the heroine and pays off in ch 29. All 19 page-level clues pay off and the remaining three are logged as series threads. C04 (the hounds), C14 (the milled silver) and C18 (Eravi's wood-road ride) pay off only by inference. The owner may want a single line on the page for each before release.
